extracted.intended_audience: policy-makers, economists, reformers, and interested general readers
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating and designing public-revenue systems with emphasis on land-value taxation: i.e., judging taxes by effects on production, collectability, certainty, equity, and the special suitability of land-value (rent) taxation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canon 1 — bear lightly upon production
rubrics_metrics.description: That it bear as lightly as possible upon production—so as least to check the increase of the general fund from which taxes must be paid and the community maintained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taxes that lessen the reward of the producer or that are conditioned upon the act or tools of production discourage production (examples: taxes on manufactures, commerce, capital, improvements). Mode of taxation matters as much as amount; a poorly placed small tax can be more harmful than a larger properly placed one. Avoid taxes that reduce incentives to save, invest, or exert labor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canon 2 — easily and cheaply collected, fall on ultimate payers
rubrics_metrics.description: That it be easily and cheaply collected, and fall as directly as may be upon the ultimate payers—so as to take from the people as little as possible in addition to what it yields the government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer taxes which are hard to hide and easy to value and collect (land is cited as ideal: 'land cannot be hidden or carried off; its value can be readily ascertained'). Use existing collection machinery where possible to save administrative costs. Minimize intermediary shifting and administrative overhead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canon 3 — certainty
rubrics_metrics.description: That it be certain—so as to give the least opportunity for tyranny or corruption on the part of officials, and the least temptation to law-breaking and evasion on the part of the taxpayers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uncertain taxes foster corruption, evasion, and moral demoralization (examples: whisky and tobacco taxes, undervaluations at custom houses, unreliable personal-property valuations). A tax system should minimize discretion and opportunities for bribery, perjury, and fraud; certainty reduces collection costs and moral harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canon 4 — bear equally
rubrics_metrics.description: That it bear equally—so as to give no citizen an advantage or put any at a disadvantage, as compared with others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equity in incidence is essential: taxes should not arbitrarily favor particular persons or classes. Design assessments and rates to avoid unfair comparative advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxation should fall on monopolies/land value (economic rent) rather than production
rubrics_metrics.description: The value of land, or economic rent, ... expresses nothing but the advantage of appropriation. Taxes levied upon the value of land cannot check production ... Taxes may be imposed upon the value of land until all rent is taken by the State, without reducing the wages of labor or the reward of capital one iota.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer taxing land values (monopoly rent) because rent is created by community growth, not individual production; taxing it diverts monopoly gain to public uses without discouraging production. Avoid taxing patent/copyright temporary monopolies (those reward labor's intangible products) but see permanent appropriation-generated rents as fair targets. A full land-value tax would prevent speculative withholding of land and stimulate productive use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid taxes on production, processes, capital, improvements, and commerce
rubrics_metrics.description: All taxes upon manufactures, all taxes upon commerce, all taxes upon capital, all taxes upon improvements, are of this kind [that check production]. Their tendency is the same ... they have a tendency to reduce the production of wealth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such taxes interpose artificial obstacles to creation of wealth (examples: taxes on ship-building, duties that raise prices and destroy exchanges). Where possible, substitute taxes on monopoly rents/land values for these taxes to avoid discouraging productive activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax incidence should not be shifted into higher prices
rubrics_metrics.description: A tax on land values does not add to prices, and is thus paid directly by the persons on whom it falls; whereas, all taxes upon things of unfixed quantity increase prices, and in the course of exchange are shifted from seller to buyer, increasing as they go.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design taxes so they are borne directly rather than being passed on through prices, which multiplies the burden across the chain and raises consumer costs (example: import duties inflated into retail prices). Land-value taxes avoid this cascading price effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxes should destroy speculative rent and open unused land to use
rubrics_metrics.description: If land were taxed to anything near its rental value, no one could afford to hold land that he was not using, and, consequently, land not in use would be thrown open to those who would use it. Settlement would be closer ... labor and capital would be enabled to produce much more with the same exertion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A desirable property of taxation is that it discourage speculative holding of land, prevent vacant/idle lots, and thereby stimulate production and employment. This is an intended economic effect to look for when evaluating tax proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security for improvements is the necessary condition for proper land use
rubrics_metrics.description: What is required for the improvement of land is not absolute ownership of the land, but security for the improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy should ensure that those who invest labor or capital on land have secure claim to the fruits of their improvement (examples: leases, fixed ground rent terms, vakouf arrangements, joint-stock holding of real estate). Full private title to land is not necessary to induce improvement; protecting improvement-rights suffices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical method: appropriate rent by taxation instead of confiscating land
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not necessary to purchase or to confiscate private property in land. ... It is only necessary to confiscate rent. ... To abolish all taxation save that upon land values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation guidance: do not aim at mass dispossession; use existing tax machinery to appropriate land rent, gradually replace other taxes with a land-value tax. Leave owners' nominal title and transactions intact while diverting economic rent to public revenue.
